description: A two-panel composite figure, both panels being data plots relating stacking fault energy (SFE) to dislocation behaviour in austenitic steel. (a) is a scatter plot with overlaid calculated curves: y-axis is "Partial Dislocation Separation (nm)" spanning 2-12, x-axis is "Dislocation Angle (deg.)" spanning 0-90 with ticks every 30°. Measured data are open triangles (2.5 Si), open circles (Base) and open squares (2.5 Al); a boxed legend headed "Alloy SFE (mJ/m²)" prints 2.5 Si 19.9 ± 2.0, Base 26.3 ± 3.0 and 2.5 Al 38.3 ± 6.1. Solid lines are the calculated trends based on each alloy's average SFE, dashed lines the upper and lower bounds from the SFE standard deviation. Partial dislocation separation increases with dislocation angle for all three alloys, being highest for 2.5 Si and lowest for 2.5 Al at any given angle. (b) is an error-bar plot of "Stacking Fault Energy (mJ/m²)" (roughly 15-50) versus "Relative Alloying (wt pct)" (0-3), with points for Base at 0 wt.%, and 2.5 Al and 2.5 Si at about 2.5 wt.%; two horizontal dashed lines mark the base level and a lower level. The pair of panels shows that Al alloying raises SFE while Si alloying lowers it, and that this SFE difference drives the observed partial dislocation spacings.

subfigures.description: Scatter plot of partial dislocation separation (nm, y-axis 2-12) versus dislocation angle (deg., x-axis 0-90) for three alloys: open triangles = 2.5 Si, open circles = Base, open squares = 2.5 Al. Boxed legend 'Alloy SFE (mJ/m²)' gives 2.5 Si 19.9 ± 2.0, Base 26.3 ± 3.0, 2.5 Al 38.3 ± 6.1. Solid lines = calculated trends from average SFE; dashed lines = upper/lower bounds from SFE standard deviation. Separation rises with angle for every alloy, highest for 2.5 Si, lowest for 2.5 Al.

Error-bar plot of stacking fault energy (mJ/m², y-axis about 15-50) versus relative alloying (wt pct, x-axis 0-3). Base point at 0 wt.% near 26 mJ/m², 2.5 Al point at about 2.5 wt.% near 38 mJ/m² with the largest error bar, 2.5 Si point at about 2.5 wt.% near 20 mJ/m². Two horizontal dashed reference lines frame the base value.

observations.observation: Panel (a) axes are 'Partial Dislocation Separation (nm)' (2-12) versus 'Dislocation Angle (deg.)' (0-90).
The boxed legend in (a) is headed 'Alloy SFE (mJ/m²)' and lists 2.5 Si 19.9 ± 2.0, Base 26.3 ± 3.0 and 2.5 Al 38.3 ± 6.1.
In (a) the 2.5 Si data are open triangles, the Base data open circles and the 2.5 Al data open squares.
Partial dislocation separation increases monotonically with dislocation angle for all three alloys, with 2.5 Si highest and 2.5 Al lowest at a given angle.
The solid lines are the calculated trends based on the calculated average SFE for each material and the dashed lines are the upper and lower bounds from the calculated SFE standard deviation.
Panel (b) plots 'Stacking Fault Energy (mJ/m²)' against 'Relative Alloying (wt pct)' over an x-range of 0-3 wt.%.
In (b) the Base point lies at 0 wt.% alloying near 26 mJ/m², the 2.5 Al point near 2.5 wt.% at about 38 mJ/m² with the widest error bar, and the 2.5 Si point near 2.5 wt.% at about 20 mJ/m².
Two horizontal dashed lines in (b), the upper near the base SFE value and the lower near 23 mJ/m², provide reference levels.
2.5 wt.% Al alloying increases the SFE by 12.0 mJ m⁻² relative to the base alloy, while 2.5 wt.% Si alloying decreases it by 6.4 mJ m⁻².
The base alloy SFE is 26.3 mJ m⁻², said to be consistent with 30 mJ m⁻² reported for a similar 15 Ni-11 Cr alloy from TEM analysis of extended dislocation nodes.

The Williams and Carter partial-dislocation strain-field correction was not applied; an upper-limit estimate would raise the 2.5 Al SFE to 44.0 ± 9.8 mJ m⁻² while other alloys change by about 1 mJ m⁻² or less.
Figure 3(b) shows the dependence of SFE on relative Si and Al alloying.
